purpose: One row per discrete physical object. The per-item asset campaign runs one agent per row. Class-level agents produced placement systems; this manifest produces objects.
laws: Everything is BUILT BY HAND, procedurally, in Blender. No downloaded models, no photo textures, no HDRIs, no AI-generated anything. The project is currently clean - verified zero image-texture nodes. Keep it that way.
No real sponsor names, no real team liveries. 31 invented brands already exist in build_dressing's brand book and 12 are shared with build_architecture - reuse them.
Scale against the measured car: 5.698 m long, 2.005 m wide, 0.340 m ride height.
z = 0.000 is simultaneously the showroom floor, the paddock apron, the access road and the pit-straight racing surface. One plane, no lip, no step.
Everything standing on ground embeds >= 0.020 m (BASE_EMBED_M) and is placed with world_contract.world_ground_z, never on an assumed z.
Every object is recentred on emit and every material reads TexCoord->Object, never Geometry->Position: at |P| ~ 1000 m a position-driven procedural loses all precision.
Chunk along s so no object spans more than ~80-260 m of circuit.

camera_model.derivation: nearest_camera_m is DERIVED, not guessed: a 4,507-sample camera corridor was built from beat_sheet.json's 16 Beat-1 keys and 8 Beat-6 keys, circuit_spec's transit legs, the doppler hover station, and circuit_spec's explicit Beat-5 vantage table (chase s0-760; kerb-height hairpin station s760-1160 on the INSIDE kerb of T4 at z=+0.85; helicopter arc s1160-1910; dive to the sweeper s1910-2403; under Le Pont de la Plongee then the hover s2403-2700; whip-and-catch 485 m chord s2700-3115; onboard follow s3115-3675 at 1.9 m). Distances are the minimum over that corridor.

beat5_vantages.phase: kerb-height hairpin pass (STATIC on the T4 inside kerb, z=+0.85, 21 mm)
rise + helicopter arc over the infield bowl
under Le Pont de la Plongee (~5 m alt, 300 km/h) then the doppler hover at s=2555

zones.name: Showroom envelope & the breach
zones.note: Beats 1-3 + the Beat-6 held frame. World origin, 34x26 m pavilion, glazed bay GW_Right on X=+15. The lens is inside this box for the first 44 s of the film and comes back to it as the last image.

zones.name: Transit corridor: glass to merge
zones.note: The 244.3 m access ribbon, world X=+15 to the pit-exit merge at (161.02, 35.09). Four thresholds in 5.6 s: breach plane, walled corridor, portal at X=+58, pit-wall line, blend line. Camera crosses all of it.

zones.name: Paddock & transporter park
zones.note: Circuit x -480..+100, y 40.5..115 (580 x 74.5 m). Only ~6 % of it is inside 15 m of the lens - the corridor along the Beat-4 route (circuit x -360..-280) plus the showroom surround. The rest is 40-90 m background.

zones.name: Pit building & garages
zones.note: 14 bays at 22 m, circuit x -245..+75, y 23.5..40.5, roof z +12.0. Seen from Beat 4 (west bays at 10-17 m) and across the pit lane on the onboard follow (20-25 m).

zones.name: Pit lane & garage working furniture
zones.note: 12 m wide, circuit y 11.5..23.5, x -245..+130. Never closer than ~10 m; read at 10-25 m. Must be legible and correct, not micro-detailed.

zones.name: Pit straight, S/F, gantry, footbridge
zones.note: 810 m at 16 m wide, dead flat z=0.000. The onboard follow runs it at 207-323 km/h with the lens 1.9 m off the deck; the camera passes UNDER the gantry (9.0 m soffit) and UNDER La Passerelle (7.5 m soffit).

zones.name: Grandstand band
zones.note: 600 m x 28 m x 14 m, circuit y -34..-62, x -420..+180. The Beat-6 crane-out clears the roof by 13.8 m and passes the front top edge at ~9 m. Empty stands are a deliberate look - which makes every seat individually visible.

zones.name: Racing surface
zones.note: 3675 m welded cyclic mesh. The lens gets to 0.8-1.1 m of it at the hairpin station and rides 1.9 m above it for 560 m of onboard follow.

zones.name: Kerbs & painted markings
zones.note: 35 serrated kerbs, 1.50 m wide, 75 mm peak. The T4 inside kerb is the single closest piece of world geometry in the film.

zones.name: Runoff, gravel traps, verges
zones.note: 227,208 m2 of platform; 41,137 m2 of gravel; 50,072 m2 of tarmac runoff. The doppler hover stands ON the right-hand verge at 2.4 m.

zones.name: Barriers & catch fencing
zones.note: 1,821 W-beam panels, 3,641 posts, 5,611 TecPro blocks, 690 fence posts, 2,255 tyres. The doppler hover sits 4.2-4.4 m off the armco and fence it looks past.

zones.name: Le Pont de la Plongee
zones.note: 30 m span, 6 m deck, soffit +6.80 over s=2410. The camera threads UNDER it at ~5 m altitude and 300 km/h with 1.8 m of clearance - the soffit fills the frame.

zones.name: Trackside dressing
zones.note: 25 marshal posts, 584 barrier boards, 80 fence banners, 13 hoardings, 24 braking boards, 15 corner plates, 15 TV masts, 129 tyre stacks.

zones.name: Terrain, treeline & ground cover
zones.note: 24,622 woodland trees, 38,738 shrubs, 1,432,086 grass clumps. Grass reaches 3.5 m of the lens at s=2502 and sits directly under the doppler hover at 2.4 m.

zones.name: Figures
zones.note: A private shakedown, not a race meeting: empty grandstands, a manned marshal chain, a small crew presence in the paddock, two or three photographers. Everyone trackside is fully covered - overalls, helmet, gloves - which is what makes them tractable.

zones.name: Crowd & spectator infrastructure
zones.note: A RACE WEEKEND, not a private test. 18,350 seats at 82 % occupancy = 15,050 figures in the 600 m grandstand band, plus general-admission banking at six corners. Nearest seated spectator is 14.7 m under the Beat-6 crane-out; the closest civilians in the entire film are the ones leaning over La Passerelle's parapet at 7.1 m, seen from directly underneath.

zones.name: The ephemeral
zones.note: Litter, stains, marbles, tape, chalk. Individually trivial; collectively the difference between a render and a place.

build_waves.1: Foundations and the closest heroes: <= 4 m from the lens, or depended on by >= 4 other items.
build_waves.2: <= 10 m, or depended on by >= 2 other items.

items.name: Showroom floor slab
items.notes: 30.0 x 22.0 m, top z=0.000 exactly - same plane as the paddock apron and the pit straight. Round-1 geometry, transform IDENTITY. In Beat 1 it is the mirror every part is presented against.

items.name: Glass shard
variation_axes: laminate interlayer still bridging two plates on ~15 % of shards
items.notes: The money object of Beat 3. Must have real thickness, ground edges catching the low sun, and an interlayer that stretches rather than snaps on the laminated fraction. Wrong version: flat triangles with no thickness - they vanish edge-on and the field reads as confetti.

items.name: T4 apex kerb (hero)
items.notes: THE closest piece of world geometry in the entire film: the static camera sits ON this kerb at z=+0.85 with a 21 mm lens. A 75 mm serration is 210 px tall. Every arris, every chip, every trapped stone is on camera for 3.9 s while the car yaws 176 degrees. Nothing else in the world is under this much scrutiny.

items.name: Persistent floor shards inside the showroom
items.notes: Continuity requirement: if the camera ever sees the showroom again it is wounded. These stay for the rest of the film.

items.name: Portal signage & gate number
items.notes: Legible at 1.0 m. Invented names only.

items.name: Asphalt wearing course
items.notes: 11 detail scales already exist, 140 m down to 0.6 mm. The lens reaches 1.1 m at the hairpin, and rides 1.9 m for 560 m at 323 km/h. KNOWN LIMIT: displacement is bump-only (1-3 mm of relief). If the hairpin frames show flat aggregate at 1.1 m, this is the first thing to promote to true displacement - and then it must be re-checked for TEMPORAL flicker in motion, not just in a still.

items.name: Rubbered-in racing line
variation_axes: width by corner (heart 0.55 x spread, feather to 0.78 x half-width)
tyre tracks at +/-0.82 m, 0.20 m wide
items.notes: Measured reflectance 0.0281-0.0288 rubbered vs 0.0626-0.0808 clean, ratio 2.23-2.87. THE OUT LAP IS NOT THE FLYING LAP: at s=0 the drawn rubber sits at u=-4.8 while the transit blend puts the car on the centreline. That is correct and must not be 'fixed'.

items.name: Track-edge white line
items.notes: Paint has THICKNESS (3.5 mm on the grid numerals). At 1.1 m a zero-thickness line is a decal.

items.name: Paver mat longitudinal joint
items.notes: The single most convincing asphalt detail there is: real tracks are laid in 9.5 m mats and the joints run the length of the circuit. Wrong version: no joints at all, which is what 'flat grey paving' means.

items.name: Green painted verge strip
variation_axes: 1.0 m wide with a 100 mm white line on the inboard lip
items.notes: Outboard of every kerb. This is painted ASPHALT, not grass - do not plant it.

items.name: Sill extrusion & base reveal
items.notes: The camera passes over this at 1.3 m on the way out. Pressure-equalised sill with weep slots and setting blocks visible where glass is gone.

items.name: Turntable dais deck
items.notes: 7.4 m diameter platform, 6.9 m deck, top z=+0.340. Ride height is 0.340 m - the deck top and the car's floor are the same number, which is the scale key for the whole showroom.

items.name: Dais delivery ramp
items.notes: NEW BUILD, explicitly called out in circuit_spec: 0.340 m rise over 2.60 m (13.1 %), full 3.0 m width, X=+3.70 to +6.30. Without it the car steps off a 340 mm cliff at launch.

items.name: Pit-exit portal frame
items.notes: At world X=+58, clear width 2.6 m margin. THE CAMERA PASSES THROUGH IT - closest approach 0.0 m. Whatever this is made of will fill the frame for two frames at 4K.

items.name: Tyre marble
items.notes: Individual pellets, not a texture. They bank OFF-line, which is exactly where the camera slides during the outboard-alongside chase at T1/T2.

items.name: Patch repair
items.notes: ~25 per lap. A patch that is only a colour change is a decal; it needs a saw-cut edge, a sealant bead and a millimetre of settlement.

items.name: Dust & grit drift at the kerb line
variation_axes: accumulation in the lee of kerbs and posts
swept lines where a car has passed
items.notes: 1.5 m from the lens at the hairpin. Nothing makes a kerb look bedded-in like the grit that has collected against it.

items.name: Curtain-wall mullion
items.notes: 0.075 x 0.160 x 6.200 m at 2.20 m centres; one sits exactly on the launch axis Y=0. Extruded aluminium: thermal break, screw ports, gasket races. Wrong version: a plain box.

items.name: Curtain-wall glass panel (pre-fractured)
variation_axes: shard size gradient (fine at impact, coarse at edges)
items.notes: 2.125 x 5.980 m, laminated. Cell-fracture with the seed density falling off from the launch axis Y=0. Wrong version: uniform Voronoi across the whole pane - real toughened glass dices near the strike and holds slabs at the frame. Edges must be conchoidal and thickness-visible (10-12 mm), not zero-thickness planes.

items.name: Glazing gasket, setting blocks & silicone bead
items.notes: EPDM wedge gasket + structural silicone. At 1.6 m on a 58 mm lens a 20 mm gasket is ~130 px - the seam between glass and metal must be a real detail, not a shared vertex.

items.name: Access-road concrete slab
items.notes: 12.0 m wide, 244.3 m long; the first 49.6 m is DEAD FLAT at z=0.000. Unrubbered concrete: it must not carry the track's rubber line. Wrong version: same asphalt shader as the circuit.

items.name: Forecourt paving bay
items.notes: The apron the car lands on. Bay module and joint pattern must survive a 1.7 m lens - a single unbroken slab reads as lino.

items.name: Saw-cut joint & sealant
items.notes: The rhythm that tells you it is concrete and not tarmac at 1.7 m.

items.name: Exterior ground apron
items.notes: Round-1 ExteriorGround must be re-levelled from z -0.14..-0.08 to EXACTLY 0.000 over world X 10..90, Y -40..+40, blended over a further 20 m. A 140 mm step here is a visible kerb the car jumps.

items.name: Weed in a joint
items.notes: 1.7 m from the lens on the forecourt. Weeds in saw joints are the single strongest 'this place is real' signal in the whole paddock.

items.name: Apron retaining wall panel (north)
items.notes: 2.40 m cut-faced concrete at +8.0 m offset over the middle 90 m. The camera passes 1.8 m from it at ~130 km/h - form-tie holes and lift lines are what stop it looking like grey plastic.

items.name: Le Pont de la Plongee - deck soffit
items.notes: THE CAMERA THREADS UNDER THIS AT 1.8 m OF CLEARANCE AT 300 km/h. Soffit at +6.80 over s=2410, camera at ~5 m. It fills the frame for about 8 frames and it is the last thing before the doppler hover. A blank grey plane here is a hole in the film.

items.name: Apron wall coping & oversail
items.notes: 0.16 m coping oversail. Reads as a hard sunlit line the whole length of the corridor.

items.name: Soffit service duct & cable tray
items.notes: At 1.8 m this is what the audience actually sees of the bridge.

items.name: Ground dust burst at the breach
items.notes: Driven by the sim contact frame, not hand-timed.

items.name: Weep pipe & staining
items.notes: Every 4th panel. Tiny, and it is the detail that dates the wall.

items.name: Concrete spall & secondary debris
items.notes: Skitters across the concrete outside. Reads as the wall having structure behind the glass.

items.name: Lock-up / flat-spot mark
variation_axes: the double stripe of a locked front pair

items.name: Portal boom gate (raised)
items.notes: Parked up. Tells you the corridor is normally closed.

items.name: Start/finish line paint
variation_axes: the 6.75 mm datum step under it
items.notes: CONTRACT DEFECT to be aware of: the ground datum steps 6.75 mm across s=0 because the undulation noise is not cyclic. It hides under this 400 mm of paint, but the onboard follow crosses here at 323 km/h.

items.name: Timing loop saw cut & resin
items.notes: At s=0, 1200 and 2450 (the sector splits). The camera crosses s=0 at 1.9 m.

items.name: Barrier-face advertising board
items.notes: Mounted 50 mm PROUD of the barrier face - that standoff shadow is what makes it a board and not a painted stripe. Runs of 9-46 m, skipped over concrete.

items.name: Terrain ground surface
variation_axes: 8 baked vertex attributes: wet, wear, cover, mown, hedge, dry, field (RGB crop), dist
items.notes: 805 x 793 grid over 21.7 x 21.7 km. The doppler hover stands 2.4 m above it. KNOWN LIMIT: slope is not baked as a vertex attribute - it is read from the shading normal at render time. Also: every terrain material must be RE-CHECKED against the contract's lambert_radiance, because terrain's own lighting assumptions (direct:diffuse 3.00:1) are superseded by the measured 2.072:1 - shadows are 45 % brighter relative to key than the turf albedo was tuned for. That mismatch is the direct cause of the 'pink and green blotches'.

items.name: Grass clump - fescue
variation_axes: wind lean 15 deg x 0.55-1.55 on bearing 65 deg
items.notes: 467 px tall directly under the doppler hover, and 3.5 m from the lens at s=2502. Blades must resolve individually there. 460 clumps per station-metre per side, ~9/m2 at the verge falling to ~2 at 46 m out.

items.name: Serrated kerb unit
items.notes: 1.50 m wide, 25 mm proud track-side, 50 mm outer, 25 mm serration on 250 mm pitch = 75 mm peak. Leaves 265 mm of plank clearance against 340 mm ride height. Wrong version: one extruded ribbon with a repeating stripe - the unit-to-unit step and roll is the whole read.

items.name: Pont de la Plongee girder
items.notes: 1.35 m deep girders, 30 m span, 6.0 m deck. Origin world (-617.56, 94.75), heading 295.4 deg.

items.name: Traffic cone
items.notes: Nothing says placeholder like a perfect cone standing perfectly upright. At least 20 % must be leaning, scuffed or knocked flat.

items.name: Curtain-wall transom rail
items.notes: 3 transoms full width. Must fracture with the assembly.

items.name: Kerb end ramp
variation_axes: impact damage at the leading arris
items.notes: The tapered terminal. Real kerbs never just stop.

items.name: Negative kerb trough
variation_axes: grit and rubber accumulation in the trough
items.notes: -60 mm deep, 0.80 m wide, 1.6 m end ramps. T8 apex and T12 exit ONLY. Causes an 18 % suspension extension event against 340 mm ride height - it must be geometrically exact or the car's motion lies.

items.name: Armco W-beam panel
items.notes: ARMCO_TOP = 1.012 m (FIA 3-beam). The profile must be a true W with correct return lips - at 2.6 m from the doppler hover the section is fully readable. Incident scars are depth 10-190 mm over 5-30 m; 72 % of them on the outside.

items.name: Catch fence post
variation_axes: 6.00 m long, 1.20 m embed, 8.00 m centres
items.notes: The doppler hover sits 4.2 m from these. A post that is perfectly plumb every 8 m for 3.6 km is the tell.

items.name: Armco post
items.notes: The single most-repeated object trackside. Every post is driven, so every post has a slightly different height, lean and collar of disturbed ground. Identical posts on a perfect line is what made the round-1 barriers read as 'smeared plastic'.

items.name: Splice bolt set
items.notes: 6,862 of them and 3.5 % are missing. That deliberate absence is worth more than any shader.

items.name: Settled shard fan on the apron
variation_axes: density falls with distance from the wall
items.notes: 40+ m fan in front of the wall; must still be there in Beat 6 where it reads as a ~140 px glitter band at 595 m. Continuity: the world is wounded for the rest of the film.

items.name: Barrier scuff / paint transfer
variation_axes: height above ground matching a real contact
items.notes: Paint transfer at the right HEIGHT is the tell - it must line up with something that could have hit it.

items.name: Gravel bed surface
items.notes: 41,137 m2 over 21 beds. A flat gravel plane is the placeholder; real beds are raked, mounded at the edges and scarred where something has been recovered.

items.name: Rake furrow
items.notes: Explicitly called for. Cheap, and it makes a gravel trap read as maintained ground rather than a noise field.

items.name: Temporary (Heras) fence panel
items.notes: 3.5 x 2.0 m. Perimeter plus 3 internal runs. The lean and the gaps are the whole read.

items.name: Driver figure
variation_axes: head and shoulder movement under lateral load
items.notes: DECIDED: YES. At the T4 hairpin station the cockpit passes within ~3-5 m of a 21 mm lens for 3.9 s while the car yaws 176 degrees, and the onboard follow runs 560 m beside it - an empty seat with a slack harness would be the single most glaring hole in the film. Only the helmet, shoulders, upper arms and hands are ever visible above the cockpit rim, and every one of them is covered, so no skin and no face are needed. The head must move: it stays level under lateral load while the car rolls, and it leads the steering into an apex. A rigidly bolted head is worse than no driver. The Beat-1 tension is resolved and is NOT a build-agent problem: the 'no part seats without having been seen' law governs the 15 CAR clusters from the inventory, and the driver is not one of them - he is a person who gets in, not a part that seats. The beat-sheet owner handles it.

items.name: S/F gantry truss beam
items.notes: Soffit at z=+9.00, 2.2 m deep. THE CAMERA PASSES UNDER IT AT 3.0 m. Every bolt cluster and node plate on the underside is on camera.

items.name: Pont de la Plongee deck slab
Oil stain
variation_axes: drip pattern under a parked vehicle
items.notes: User-named. Concentrated where vehicles stand: garage floors, the transporter park, the compound.

items.name: Access-road kerb unit
items.notes: Half-battered kerb, dropped at the crossings. Individual units, not an extruded ribbon.

items.name: Track-edge slot drain & grating
variation_axes: one grating in 7 sits ~16 mm low
items.notes: The rebate ring is the object. A grating flush with the asphalt reads as a printed pattern.

items.name: Barrier foot kerb / edge beam
items.notes: 439 m of ARCH_RetainEdge exists as a cast edge beam with weep pipes every 4th panel and a bollard where the drop exceeds 280 mm. Keep the rule: nothing where the drop is under 10 mm.

items.name: Breach dust column (volume)
items.notes: 20-25 m column, still settling 90 s later so it is present in the Beat-6 hold. Must be a LOCAL volume: the global haze slabs have visible_shadow=False and cast no god rays.

items.name: Heavy rubber cable ramp
items.notes: The single most paddock-looking object there is. Must deform where vehicles cross it.

items.name: Cigarette end
items.notes: User-named. Clusters near doorways, gates and the smoking side of every building - never uniform.

items.name: Driver gloves
items.notes: Hands on the wheel at 3 m. The SW cluster already resolves to macro standard - gloves that do not match that standard will be the weak point of the frame.

items.name: Driver helmet
items.notes: 209 px at 3.0 m through a 21 mm lens at the hairpin station. The tear-off stack on the visor and the raking reflection across it are the two things that make a helmet look like it is being worn rather than displayed. Invented livery only.

items.name: Driver race suit & HANS
variation_axes: shoulder and collar folds under the belts
items.notes: Only the shoulders, upper arms and the top of the chest are ever visible above the cockpit rim - build for that framing. The belt-over-shoulder compression is the detail.

items.name: Forecourt bollard
items.notes: At world X=19.5, Y=+/-9.0. Cast or stainless sleeve over a core; the car threads between them.

items.name: Gaffer tape on the ground
variation_axes: lifted edge with grit under it
items.notes: User-named. The lifted, gritty edge is the object; a flat rectangle is a decal.

items.name: Gantry soffit panel & services
items.notes: The single most-overlooked hero surface in the film: you only ever see the underside, at 3 m, at 4K.

items.name: Gravel retaining kerbstone
items.notes: The lip between the asphalt runoff and the gravel bed. Without it the two surfaces just abut, which is the giveaway.

items.name: Fence banner scrim
variation_axes: sun bleach on the south face
items.notes: On ~35 % of panels. Must sag between ties and flap-crease, not stretch flat.

items.name: Pit-exit gore chevrons
variation_axes: 0.30 m paint on 1.20 m pitch at 45 deg

items.name: Pont de la Plongee fascia banner
Deck scupper & downpipe
items.notes: The stain below a scupper is the cheapest realism on any bridge.

items.name: Puddle
items.notes: Sits in the low points the drainage model already defines - swales, gully surrounds, settled paving bays. A puddle placed anywhere else contradicts the ground.

items.name: Rust streak from a fixing
variation_axes: running down a vertical vs pooling on a horizontal

items.name: Grass runoff turf
variation_axes: 8 baked attributes (wet, wear, cover, mown, dry)
items.notes: 18-25 m of it as the default runoff, and 20 m at T5. The rejected renders showed this as 'pink and green blotches' - the fix is that the ground shader and the clump geometry have to agree, not fight.

items.name: Tarmac runoff mat
variation_axes: different mix from the track (paler, coarser)
paver joints at a different angle
items.notes: 50,072 m2. It must NOT look like the racing surface - real runoff is a coarser, lighter mix laid in different mats, and the moment it matches the track the width of the circuit becomes unreadable.

items.name: Transit tyre wall (south)
items.notes: 2.00 m stack at -7.0 m offset over 84 m. South clearance narrows to 1.737 m at route t=90 - the camera is close to this.

items.name: Transit debris fence (over the tyre wall)
items.notes: Reaches 4.30 m total. Backlit by the low sun for the whole corridor run.

items.name: Facade cladding panel (anodised)
items.notes: Reads as 33 px of facade at the Beat-6 hold (595 m) but at 3.6 m in Beat 4. The panel joint rhythm is the only thing that gives the building scale at both ends.

items.name: Grid numeral paint
items.notes: Depends on Blender's bundled vector font; if it is unavailable the numerals are skipped and the boxes still build. Verify it renders.

items.name: Grid launch rubber stripe
items.notes: 20 pairs. Already built; the pair spacing must match the measured 2.005 m car width.

items.name: Tyre wall tyre
variation_axes: compression flat at the bottom of a stack
items.notes: 370 px at 4 m from the T4 hairpin station. The tyres BEHIND the hairpin camera are in shot the whole time the car yaws. Compression flattening down a stack and the dark water line inside the bead are the two details that sell it.

items.name: Conveyor belt facing
items.notes: The rubber conveyor belt strapped across the face. Its sag between bolts is the difference between a tyre wall and a stack of doughnuts.

items.name: Bent mullion stub (survivor)
variation_axes: paint craze at the plastic hinge
items.notes: The two at Y=+/-4.4 survive the 9.6 m aperture as bent stubs. Plastic hinge with local buckling of the extrusion walls - not a smooth bend. This is the object that tells the audience how big the hole is.

items.name: Paper / wrapper litter
variation_axes: drift into corners and against kerbs
items.notes: Drifts where wind and geometry put it - against the windward face of barriers and in the lee of every post. Scattered uniformly is the placeholder.

items.name: Road gully & grating
variation_axes: 1 in 7 sits ~16 mm low, 1 in 11 lifted
items.notes: Cast frame with a 14 mm rebate ring. The recess is the detail; a flush grating reads as a decal.

items.name: Armco terminal end
items.notes: A barrier run that stops square is a placeholder. Terminals ramp, flare or turn away.

items.name: Discarded bottle
items.notes: The user named it. One discarded bottle, correctly weathered and correctly placed, does more than a thousand instanced clean ones.

items.name: Driver boots
items.notes: Barely visible in the footwell, but the footwell is modelled (CI_footwell) and an empty one is worse than a cheap boot.

items.name: Facade signage (invented marque)
items.notes: Invented brand only. No real marque. Must read at 4 m in Beat 4 and survive being 2 px wide in Beat 6.

items.name: Wall framing behind the glazing
items.notes: Must pre-fracture with the wall - the brief says 'plus wall framing'. Exposed studwork inside the wound in Beats 4 and 6.

items.name: Paddock paving bay
items.notes: 5,560 bays over 49,645 m2. Bay-to-bay height variation must stay inside +/-15 mm - measured max is +14.8 mm today, and the tolerance is 15.5 mm.

items.name: Marshal post platform deck
variation_axes: 4 archetypes (open canopy, box hut, equipment stand, raised platform)
items.notes: 25 posts, max gap 253.9 m, min sight-line clearance +0.41 m. The rejected render showed this as flat cardboard - it needs board gaps, a wear path, and things stored under the deck.

items.name: Pit wall precast unit
items.notes: 375 m of wall, face pinned on circuit y=+11.500. The step and tilt between units IS the object - a continuous extrusion reads as a plastic kerb from the onboard follow.

items.name: Team truck trailer
items.notes: A 14 m flank at 8 m is 2/3 of the frame height. It cannot be a coloured box - it needs panel joints, rivet lines, kick plates, dirt gradient rising from the road.

items.name: Crew fireproof overall
items.notes: THE garment that makes the whole crew work. Nomex hangs stiffer than cotton - fewer, larger folds, and it holds a crease at the elbow and the back of the knee. Get the fold LANGUAGE right once here and 110 figures inherit it.

items.name: Team timing stand
items.notes: NOT IN THE SPEC AND NOT BUILT - a genuine gap. A pit wall with no timing stands is the clearest sign nobody is home.

items.name: Tyre blanket
items.notes: User-named class. A blanket that is a smooth cylinder is wrong - it must bulge over the tyre and gape at the seam.

items.name: Spectator - seated
variation_axes: lean forward / back / turned to a neighbour / arms folded / arms up
build and stature spread including 8 % children
items.notes: 254 px tall, head 47 px, at the closest point of the Beat-6 crane-out. NO FACES: at 47 px a head is a hair shape, a skin value and a suggestion of features - modelling eyes and mouths is wasted work and will read worse than a clean silhouette. Spend the budget on POSTURE and SILHOUETTE instead. Torso angle, shoulder line, knee position and where the arms are is 100 % of the read. A stand where every figure has the same shoulder angle is the crowd equivalent of one tree spammed a hundred times.

items.name: Terrace riser unit (precast)
items.notes: 816 sawn bays. Still hero: the riser fronts, the gangways and the tread strips are exactly the parts the crowd does NOT cover, and from directly above they are the grid the whole crowd is registered against.

items.name: Catch fence mesh panel
items.notes: KNOWN APPROXIMATION: the weave is ANALYTIC everywhere except the doppler window (s 2495-2615, side -1) where real 3-D wire is built. The arcminute argument is 4.5 arcmin (3.5 px) per wire at 4 m - so the analytic version is defensible, but set_fence_fade(scene) MUST be called by the render orchestrator or the weave resolves wrong at non-4K sizes.

items.name: Woven wire (real 3-D)
variation_axes: 5.2 mm wire, 0.050 pitch, 10.4 % coverage per layer, 19.7 % combined
items.notes: Only in WIRE_WINDOWS (s 2495-2615, side -1) - the doppler hover looks THROUGH this at the car. It is 4.2 m from the lens and backlit by a 12.5 deg sun. This is the one place the analytic cheat would be caught.

items.name: Head extrusion
items.notes: 21.919 m of head. Carries the panels' top edge; tears out where the aperture forms.

items.name: Verge drainage swale
variation_axes: standing water in the low points
items.notes: 0.34 m swale 7 m beyond the platform edge. It is what makes the ground read as drained rather than extruded.

items.name: Downpipe, hopper & gutter
items.notes: Cheap to build, and the thing whose absence makes a building read as a box.

items.name: La Passerelle deck
items.notes: Circuit x=-450, soffit 7.50 m, 4.0 m deep, 52 m span. The onboard follow passes under it 1.3 s in at ~230 km/h - the soffit is 5.6 m from the lens.

items.name: Marshal overall, gloves & helmet
items.notes: The garment is the character. Cloth fold at the elbow, knee and waist is 100 % of the read at 6 m.

items.name: La Passerelle mesh screen
items.notes: Anti-throw screening. At 6 m the aperture must be real geometry or an honest arcminute-argued shader - it is backlit.

items.name: Marshal flag (set)
variation_axes: yellow, double yellow, blue, red, white, green, chequered, oil
items.notes: Seven distinct flags. A rolled flag is a soft cylinder with a taper and a loose tail, not a tube.

items.name: La Passerelle fascia banner
variation_axes: sun bleach on the south face

items.name: Broom, shovel & rake
items.notes: Leaning against the post. Cheap, and it is the single clearest sign a place is used.

items.name: Marshal - flagging
variation_axes: flag furled and held / raised / waved
items.notes: One per post, and the pose must be turned UP-TRACK - a marshal facing the wrong way is a defect anybody notices.

items.name: Marshal - standing
variation_axes: posture (watching / turned / holding a flag / on the phone)
items.notes: 261 px at 25 m, and 6.0 m at the T4 inside post. Fully covered - overall, gloves, helmet or balaclava - so no skin is needed, which is what makes this tractable. Two marshals in identical poses is worse than one.

items.name: Marshal post number sign
items.notes: 'POSTE 7'. Small, and it is the thing that names the place.

items.name: Trackside tyre stack
items.notes: 129 stacks / 543 tyres at gates, post pads and 4 service laybys. A toppled stack is worth ten upright ones.

items.name: Pit wall tapered terminal & nose board
items.notes: The west terminal is 6.1 m from the lens in Beat 4. A wall that just stops is the placeholder; a real one steps down over 7 lifts onto a spread footing with a chevron nose board.

items.name: Safety car
items.notes: 773 px at 7.0 m - the camera passes it on the Beat-4 merge. A race weekend parks it at the pit exit and this film's route goes straight past. It is a full road-car build at hero fidelity: glazing with real thickness, an interior behind the glass, panel gaps, and a light bar.

items.name: La Passerelle crowd at the parapet
variation_axes: leaning over / standing back / holding a phone or camera over the rail
hands and forearms on the rail
items.notes: THE CLOSEST CIVILIAN FIGURES IN THE FILM at 7.1 m - but the geometry is kind: the camera is 1.9 m off the deck passing UNDERNEATH at ~230 km/h, so these are seen from a steep low angle THROUGH the anti-throw mesh, and at 64 m/s with a 180-degree shutter they smear 1.33 m per frame. What actually reads is: undersides of forearms on the rail, chins and hat brims, phones held out over the parapet, and legs behind the mesh. Build for that view - do not build faces for a view that never sees them.

items.name: TecPro block (blue body)
variation_axes: UV chalking on the sun face
items.notes: T1, T4 and T12 (three-layer at T4 and T12). Real TecPro is a closed-cell foam core in a polyethylene shell with visible mould seams, lifting handles and bolt bosses. A smooth blue box is the placeholder.

items.name: Truck tyre
variation_axes: tread pattern (steer rib vs drive block)
items.notes: The user named this one explicitly. 315/70R22.5, ~1.05 m OD. Sidewall lettering must be RAISED geometry or a real displacement, and the tread must be modelled, not bumped - at 8 m a bumped tread reads as a sticker.

items.name: Team truck tractor unit
variation_axes: wash line on the lower panels
items.notes: The 'haul' the user named. Cab glazing must have real thickness and interior behind it - at 8 m an empty black cab reads as a toy.

items.name: Water bottle
items.notes: User-named. 112 px at 8 m on a 35 mm lens. Fill level and a slightly crushed body are the whole job - a rigid full cylinder is the placeholder.

items.name: Steer wheel & hub
items.notes: Wheel nut indicators (the little yellow arrows) are the detail people recognise without knowing why.

items.name: Slot drain & grating
variation_axes: 1 in 7 sits 16 mm low, 1 in 11 lifted

items.name: Shrub - bramble
items.notes: OPEN ITEM: all 5 shrub species come from ONE generator with different parameters, unlike the 10 independent tree structures. build_terrain's own note: 'if the camera ever gets within ~15 m of the undergrowth, that is the layer to rebuild next.' It does - the paddock planters are at 14 m and the verge shrubs at ~8 m.

items.name: TecPro block (red cap course)
variation_axes: as blue, plus faster UV fade on the red pigment

items.name: Truck livery decal panel
items.notes: NO real teams, NO real sponsors. Wrap seams over rivets are what make a wrap read as a wrap.

items.name: Mud flap
items.notes: User-named. It must HANG - a flat rectangle at 90 degrees is the tell.

items.name: Gravel stone
items.notes: 130,000 in the hero beds. KNOWN LIMIT: gravel below 11 mm is shader, not geometry - the documented rule is that if a lens gets inside ~0.6 m of a bed the hero tier must be raised and the bed re-run. Current closest is 2.8 m, so the rule holds, but check T1 at s=252.

items.name: Parapet coping
items.notes: Parapet at z=+10.40 - the silhouette line in the Beat-6 held frame.

items.name: Roof sheet (profiled metal)
items.notes: The single largest surface in the Beat-6 frame at t=0. Streaking below the side laps is what stops a metal roof looking like grey plastic.

items.name: Roof truss
items.notes: Seen from ABOVE at 9.5 m in Beat 6 - the top chord and the purlins are the visible faces, which is the opposite of the usual assumption.

items.name: Handheld fire extinguisher
items.notes: Everywhere: marshal posts, garages, paddock, fire points. 90+ instances and they must not all be identical.

items.name: Bin liner
items.notes: Cloth-sim or sculpted sag over the rim. A liner that ends flush with the rim is the placeholder tell.

items.name: Trash can (paddock bin)
items.notes: THE reference object for this whole campaign - the user named it by name. 296 px tall at 12 m. Every one of the four named details must be present and must differ between instances.

items.name: Wheelie bin
items.notes: User-named class. The dent in the lid and the drag scuffs on the base are the brief.

items.name: Corner name plate
variation_axes: the spec's own names disagree - T12 is 'La Plongee' / 'T12 Doppler' / 'T12 Plongee'. NORMALISE before building.
items.notes: Naming inconsistencies to resolve: T12 (three names), S4/T5 (both called 'La Rampe').

items.name: Crew gloves & boots
variation_axes: cuff over vs under the sleeve
items.notes: The cuff overlap is the detail that says the suit is worn rather than painted on.

items.name: Crew helmet, visor & balaclava
items.notes: ZERO EXPOSED SKIN on the pit-stop crew - helmet, visor, balaclava, gloves. That is precisely why these figures are tractable at 653 px while a bare-headed paddock figure at the same distance would not be.

items.name: Crew - front jack operator
variation_axes: crouched with the jack presented / lifting / stepping clear

items.name: Crew - tyre carrier (off)
variation_axes: braced to receive / arms out / tyre held at hip
items.notes: The off-carrier's whole body is a diagonal brace. Standing upright is wrong.

items.name: Crew - tyre carrier (on)
variation_axes: tyre held ready at chest / stepping in

items.name: Crew - wheel gunner
variation_axes: crouched ready / gun raised / gun down
items.notes: 653 px at 10 m. Four of them, one per corner, and the two on the far side are mirrored NOT copied - a mirrored figure with an identical fold pattern is visible. Crouched with the gun braced on the thigh is the canonical ready pose.

items.name: Braking distance marker board
items.notes: 24 boards. Full set before T1 (93.8 m stop from 330.8 km/h), 200-50 at T4, 250-50 at La Plongee, shorter sets at T5, T10, T15. Measured back from s_apex - arc/2.

items.name: Engineer on the timing stand
items.notes: Four to six per stand across ten stands. An occupied pit wall is the difference between a race weekend and a car park.

items.name: Leaf litter patch
variation_axes: species mix matching the tree above

items.name: Paddock personnel figure
items.notes: A race-weekend paddock is busy. HARDER than the trackside figures: exposed forearms, neck and face. Keep them at 10 m+, in caps and sunglasses, in groups rather than evenly spread, and never let one be the focal subject of a frame.

items.name: Press photographer at the pit wall
Rock - scree stone
variation_axes: sorting by size down a slope

items.name: Team principal on the timing stand
Pit lane surface
items.notes: 12.0 m wide. The fast lane / working lane split has to be in the surface as well as the paint.

items.name: S/F gantry leg
items.notes: Legs at circuit y=+/-11.0, 22 m clear span. The camera passes between them at 1.9 m altitude at 323 km/h.

items.name: Pedestrian crowd barrier
variation_axes: a run pushed out of line where people have leaned on it
items.notes: The interlocking hook-and-eye barrier every event on earth uses. Runs of it must NOT be a straight line - people push them.

items.name: TV camera housing
variation_axes: pan/tilt angle - they should be TRACKING THE CAR at each moment
items.notes: The one variation axis that matters here is aim: a row of cameras pointing at nothing is worse than no cameras.

items.name: Trackside TV camera mast
items.notes: One per ~245 m, biased to corner outsides.

items.name: Marshal access gate
items.notes: 28 gates from 16 GATE_STATIONS. Marshal posts within 55 m of a station are pulled to it, so gates and posts read as one facility.

items.name: Wheel gun
items.notes: User-named. Nose-mounted socket, trigger cage, torque sleeve. It should be lying on the ground or in its cradle, not floating.

items.name: Crowd density & occupancy field
variation_axes: falloff to ~55 % at the far ends and the top rows
a few whole blocks nearly empty
items.notes: THE item that decides whether 15,050 grandstand occupants read as a crowd or as a grid of dolls. Real crowds are lumpy: people sit in groups with empty seats between groups, gangways stay clear, the expensive rows fill first, the corners of a block go last. A uniform 82 % fill is as wrong as a uniform 100 %. Build this before a single figure is placed - everything else in this zone reads off it.

items.name: Spectator clothing layer
variation_axes: hue distribution weighted to invented-team colours in blocks, white/grey/black/denim elsewhere
items.notes: COLOUR DISTRIBUTION IS THE CROWD'S TEXTURE. Uniform random hue reads as television static; real crowds clump into team-colour blocks against a neutral field. Invented brands and invented team colours only. Fabric needs 3-4 real fold sets - at 254 px a flat-shaded torso is visible.

items.name: Spectator - general admission, standing
variation_axes: standing / sitting on the grass / on a folding stool
coats and bags on the ground
clustered at the best sightlines and thin between
items.notes: GA banking at six corners. They cluster hard where the sightline is good and thin out to nothing 30 m either side - a uniform smear along the bank is the tell.

items.name: General admission viewing bank
variation_axes: worn desire lines up the face
grass wear rings where groups stand
items.notes: The WEAR is the object. A grassed bank with no desire lines and no bald crest has never had anybody on it.

items.name: Front safety rail
items.notes: 34 m from the racing line for the whole onboard follow, and 15.7 m under the Beat-6 crane-out. Now also the mounting line for draped crowd banners and the rail 600 standing spectators lean on, so its top rail takes hand polish and its kick panel takes scuffs.

items.name: Grandstand column
variation_axes: paint chalking on the sun face

items.name: Garage interior floor
items.notes: Seen at 20-25 m through open doors. Dark and empty is a defect; the floor graphic and the sheen carry it.

items.name: Tree - pedunculate oak
items.notes: L0 hero under 95 m has 6 branch orders and 30-57k leaves. OPEN ITEM from build_terrain: birch is 20 % of the base mix plus 7.5 % dead timber, so a quarter of every treeline is a pale stem and it reads as 'a birch wood' everywhere - the fix is to drop birch to ~0.13 and weight to oak and hawthorn.

items.name: Pit building roof deck
items.notes: Roof at z=+12.0 - in frame for the whole Beat-6 climb.

items.name: Start light panel
items.notes: NOT IN THE SPEC - the gantry is dimensioned with no signals on it. Five columns of five. Unlit for this film, which means the lens optics and hoods have to carry it, not emission.

items.name: Medical car
variation_axes: rear equipment visible through the glass

items.name: Garage door - roller shutter
items.notes: One of four door FAMILIES - they are four different meshes, not four colours. Slat curvature and the curl at the head are the read.

items.name: Crew - front wing adjuster
variation_axes: crouched at the endplate with a driver

items.name: Crew - mechanic, kneeling at the car
variation_axes: one knee / both knees / on a pad
items.notes: The garage's most common pose and the one that most obviously fails if it is a standing figure with bent legs.

items.name: Crew - mechanic, standing at the car
variation_axes: arms folded / hands on the sidepod / reaching into the airbox / carrying a panel

items.name: Crew - pit lane fire marshal
variation_axes: extinguisher held / on the ground beside
items.notes: One per box. Fully fire-kitted including a hood - the most covered figure in the film and therefore the easiest.

items.name: Crew - visor cleaner
variation_axes: reaching over the halo with a cloth on a stick

items.name: Pit box marking
variation_axes: paint wear at the gun positions

items.name: Team crew figure (fireproofs)
items.notes: The generic garage/paddock crew figure. The POSED pit-stop roles are separate rows (crew_wheel_gunner, crew_tyre_carrier_off/on, crew_jack_operator_front/rear, crew_stabiliser, crew_release_operator, crew_mechanic_kneeling/standing, crew_pitlane_fire_marshal) because a crew all standing identically is the same failure as one tree spammed a hundred times. Completely covered - helmet, visor, balaclava, fireproofs, gloves - zero exposed skin.

items.name: Crew - engineer at the monitor bank
Crew - starter operator
variation_axes: crouched at the rear with the starter shaft in

items.name: Flight case
items.notes: Butterfly latches, ball corners and extruded edging. The edging profile is the object.

items.name: Information & gate sign
variation_axes: sector split / access gate / medical point

items.name: Tree - London plane
items.notes: 26 % of the plateau/paddock mix, and the species of the 24-tree paddock avenue at 14 m.

items.name: Generator unit
items.notes: Acoustic canopy with louvres and a lifting frame. Exhaust staining above the outlet is the detail.

items.name: Media camera operator (pit lane)
variation_axes: shoulder-mounted / on a monopod / walking backwards

items.name: Paddock avenue tree
items.notes: Built at L0. The 2 young replacements in a row of mature trees is the detail that makes a planted avenue read as maintained rather than generated.

items.name: Planter shrub
items.notes: Known gap: the 5 shrub species all come from ONE generator with different parameters. This is the layer flagged for rebuild if the lens gets inside 15 m - it does, here.

items.name: Grandstand seat
variation_axes: sun bleach on the west face
items.notes: DOWNGRADED BY THE CROWD DECISION, and that saving partly pays for the crowd. With the stands at 82 % occupancy roughly three quarters of every seat is hidden behind an occupant. What still reads from the Beat-6 crane-out is: the aisle-end units, the empty seats inside the density field's gaps, the top edge of the seat back between shoulders, and the folded seats in the near-empty blocks. Build the seat back edge and the aisle-end unit properly and let the rest be simple. It is no longer the hero it was when the stands were empty.

items.name: Seat bracket & fixing
items.notes: Almost entirely occluded once the crowd is in. Low priority.

items.name: Spectator headwear
items.notes: At 47 px of head, the HAT is a bigger silhouette contributor than the face. This is where the money goes.

items.name: Handheld crowd flag
variation_axes: waved / furled / resting on a shoulder
items.notes: Must be shaped by the same 65-degree wind bearing as the grass and the sponsor flags.

items.name: Crowd idle motion layer
variation_axes: head tracking the car with a 0.2-0.5 s spread of reaction lag
a travelling wave of standing as the car passes
items.notes: WITHOUT THIS THE STAND IS A PHOTOGRAPH OF STATUES and the one-shot illusion dies at the exact moment the camera cranes out. It does not need much: sub-frame settling, heads turning to follow the car with staggered lag, and a standing wave that travels along the stand at the car's speed. Motion blur at 24 fps hides everything else. The reaction lag spread is the detail - a crowd that turns in unison is a chorus line.

items.name: Crowd litter under the seats
variation_axes: drifted to the front of each riser
items.notes: Seen from directly above at the end of the film, this is what fills the gaps between people.

items.name: Row / seat number plate
items.notes: Visible only on aisle-end units and in the empty blocks. Low priority.

items.name: Bag, coat & belongings on seats
variation_axes: folded programme wedged under a thigh
items.notes: The clutter of occupancy. A stand full of people and NO belongings is uncanny - this is the layer that says they have been sitting there for three hours.

items.name: Spectator - child
variation_axes: seated / standing on a seat / carried
ear defenders far more common than on adults
items.notes: 8 % of the crowd. Stature variation is what stops a crowd looking machine-stamped, and children are the cheapest way to get it.

items.name: Ear defenders & headphones
items.notes: Utterly characteristic of a motorsport crowd and almost never modelled. Widens the head silhouette, which is exactly the scale that reads at 14.7 m.

items.name: Spectator - seated, leaning forward
variation_axes: leaning on the row in front
head turned to follow the car
items.notes: The pose that makes a crowd look like it is WATCHING something. At the moment the car passes, the leaning fraction should rise along the stand in a wave - that is free storytelling and it costs one animated parameter.

items.name: Spectator - standing in the row
items.notes: Standing figures break the horizontal banding of a seated stand. Without them the crowd reads as corduroy.

items.name: Spectator umbrella / parasol
variation_axes: open for shade against a 12.5-degree sun
items.notes: A 12.5-degree sun means low raking light - umbrellas tilt toward it, and the shadows they throw across the seating deck are a gift.

items.name: Spectator - phone raised
variation_axes: one arm up / two hands / at chest height
items.notes: The single most contemporary crowd signal there is. A modern grandstand at the moment a car passes is a field of raised arms; a crowd with none reads as period.

items.name: Sponsor flag
items.notes: Flags must be shaped by the SAME wind bearing as the grass lean (65 deg) or the world contradicts itself.

items.name: Tool chest / roller cabinet
items.notes: Drawer front gaps and a slightly-open drawer are worth more than any amount of shader work.

items.name: Draped crowd banner
variation_axes: wind lift at a loose corner
hung over the front rail or a barrier
items.notes: Hand-lettered bedsheet banners are what tells you these are fans rather than an audience. Deliberately imperfect lettering.

items.name: Spectator - standing at the front rail
variation_axes: holding a phone or a flag
items.notes: 333 px. The front rail row is the most legible line of people in the film and it is silhouetted against the track.

items.name: Grandstand advertising banner
variation_axes: wind lift at a loose corner

items.name: Spare wing rack
items.notes: A rack of spare front wings is the single most 'F1 garage' object after the tyre stack.

items.name: Pit building west gable
items.notes: The car threads past this on the merge. It is the biggest single object in the Beat-4 frame after the showroom.

items.name: Big screen
variation_axes: content unlit or showing a flat colour field
items.notes: Race weekend only. Do NOT put live footage on it - a screen showing the film inside the film is a recursion trap and a continuity liability across one unbroken take. A dark louvred panel with a raking specular is correct and safer.

items.name: Tree - hawthorn
variation_axes: 45 % of hedgerows at 0.55-0.85 of species height

items.name: Pont de la Plongee abutment
items.notes: Abutment tops at ground_z(2410, +/-15) = +3.984 and +3.548 - they differ by 436 mm, so the two ends of this bridge are NOT symmetric. Build to the numbers.

items.name: Crew - garage technician
variation_axes: at a bench / carrying a case / at the toolboard / pushing a trolley

items.name: Terrace skirt & counterfort
items.notes: CONTRACT GAP: the terrace is a declared addendum world_contract does not carry. Terrain must build no ground inside x -426..+186, y -69.0..-28.5 and must weld to this 1.85 m skirt.

items.name: Hospitality awning canopy
items.notes: Fabric must sag and crease. A flat quad is the classic placeholder.

items.name: Recovery tractor
variation_axes: parked behind the barrier at a gate
items.notes: Parked at recovery gates. One of the most recognisable trackside objects there is and it is currently absent.

items.name: Tree - Italian cypress
variation_axes: splay at the top of older ones

items.name: Timing / scoring tower
items.notes: CAUTION: 20 m tall near the line. Re-run circuit_spec's Beat-6 raycast gate after placing it - that gate exists to protect the last image of the film from exactly this kind of late addition.

items.name: Vomitory / tunnel mouth
variation_axes: dark interior with a real ceiling
items.notes: A vomitory that is a black rectangle is a hole in the model. It needs depth, a lit far wall, and - now that this is a race weekend - people moving through it and a steward at the mouth.

items.name: Garage light batten
items.notes: Interior practicals must stay lit - the light spilling out of an open bay is what says 'occupied'.

items.name: Folding chair
items.notes: Chairs pushed in at identical angles is the single most common CG-crowd-furniture failure.

items.name: Spare car under a cover
variation_axes: fitted cover draping over wings and wheels
items.notes: Solves the 'a race garage needs a second car and we only have one car model' problem honestly and authentically: a fitted cover is what a real garage does with a spare, and it is a cloth-sim job rather than a second 617-part build.

items.name: Garage tool board
variation_axes: shadow-board outlines with tools missing from some
items.notes: The shadow board with three tools missing is a better story than a full one.

items.name: Garage curtain divider
items.notes: Drawn curtains are how a real garage hides its business, and they are the cheapest way to make an interior read as deep without modelling it.

items.name: Upper window band
items.notes: Blinds at identical heights across 14 bays is the tell.

items.name: Field boundary fence post & wire
items.notes: Cheap, and the thing that makes farmland read as farmland rather than a green noise field.

items.name: Lighting mast column
items.notes: CAUTION: circuit_spec's Beat-6 raycast gate exists specifically 'to protect the last image of the film from a late-added lighting mast'. Any mast within the south-apron or grandstand sight cone must be re-gated.

items.name: Tree - dead standing timber
items.notes: The single best silhouette element in a treeline, and the one that stops a wood looking generated.

items.name: Windsock & pole
items.notes: Must agree with the flag and grass wind direction.

items.name: Garage rear door to the paddock
Portable toilet block
items.notes: Twenty of them in a row is one of the most reliable signals that an event is happening here.

items.name: Podium backdrop
variation_axes: invented brands in a repeating tile

items.name: Tree - silver birch
variation_axes: REDUCE from 20 % to ~13 % of the base mix

items.name: Race control building
items.notes: Deliberately separate from the modular system.

items.name: T4 escarpment skyline
variation_axes: suppressed woodland on the near lip
items.notes: OPEN DEFECT from build_terrain: 'the escarpment beyond T4 does not read from the kerb-height hairpin camera - the treeline sits on the near lip and occludes it.' The whole point of the hairpin station is that the car is silhouetted against distant terrain and sky. The fix is placement: suppress woodland inside the hairpin's outward fan. This is a hero item because it is the BACKGROUND of the film's best shot.
